schema.label: Section Title
schema.help_text: Optional header displayed above the card carousel (e.g. 'Latest', 'Featured', 'This Week'). Leave empty to show no section header — useful for the top featured banner.

schema.label: Section Subtitle
schema.help_text: Optional smaller text shown below the section title. Leave empty to hide. Example: 'Catch up on what you missed'.

schema.label: Section Image
schema.help_text: Optional image for this module section — used as a banner, section header visual, or fallback placeholder when a card from the source content type has no image. Upload at least 1200x400px for best results. Leave empty to use the app's default brand placeholder.

schema.label: Card Type
schema.help_text: Visual style of the cards in this section. 'featured' = full-bleed hero image at the top of the screen (best for banners). 'large' = image-top card ~300dp wide (best for main content). 'small' = thumbnail on the left ~260dp wide (best for compact lists).

schema.label: Enabled
schema.help_text: Toggle this section on or off in the app without deleting the record. Useful for drafting new sections before they are ready to go live.

schema.label: Source Content Type
schema.help_text: The exact slug of the CMS content type whose records will be shown as cards (e.g. 'articles', 'sermons', 'workouts', 'movies'). Must match the content type slug exactly — case-sensitive.

schema.label: Title Field Key
schema.help_text: The field key from the source content type to use as the card title (e.g. 'headline', 'name', 'title'). Leave empty to show image-only cards with no title text.

schema.label: Subtitle / Preview Field Key
schema.help_text: The field key to use as the card subtitle or short preview text (e.g. 'preview', 'tagline', 'summary', 'director'). Leave empty to hide the subtitle line on the card.

schema.label: Image Field Key
schema.help_text: The key of the media field (type: media) in the source content type to use as the card image (e.g. 'cover_image', 'poster', 'thumbnail'). The app reads the URL from that field on each source record. Leave empty to fall back to the Section Image above, or a solid brand-color block if that is also empty. Recommended: upload source images at least 800x450px for featured/large and 400x400px for small.

schema.label: Category Field Key
schema.help_text: The key of the select field in the source content type that holds the category or categories for each item (e.g. 'category', 'genre', 'tags'). Supports both single-select and multi-select fields — the app handles both automatically. Leave empty to hide category chips on the card.

schema.label: Content Date
schema.help_text: The key of a date or date_time field in the source content type to display on the card (e.g. 'release_date' for movies, 'event_date' for events, 'authored_at' for articles). This is the content's own date — not the CMS record publish timestamp assigned by the backend. Leave empty to hide the date on cards.

schema.label: Max Items
schema.help_text: Maximum number of cards to show in this carousel. Defaults to 10 when left empty. Keep at or below 20 for good scroll performance. The app only requests this many items — it does not paginate within a module.

schema.label: Enabled
schema.help_text: Toggle this section on or off in the app without deleting the record. Useful for drafting new sections before they are ready to go live. Defaults to true.

schema.label: Layout Type
schema.help_text: Visual layout of this section. 'featured' = full-bleed hero with page dots, best for top banner. 'large' = horizontal scroll, image-top cards ~300dp wide. 'small' = horizontal scroll, thumbnail-left compact cards. 'image_carousel' = image-only horizontal scroll, no text on cards, best for galleries. 'stories' = circular avatars row like Instagram Stories, best for categories or authors. 'showcase' = one large hero item + smaller items row below. 'grid' = 2-column grid, best for catalogs. 'banner' = full-width promotional banner with CTA button, does not require source_content_type.

schema.label: Section Title
schema.help_text: Optional header displayed above the section (e.g. 'Latest', 'Featured', 'This Week'). Leave empty to show no section header — typical for the top 'featured' banner or 'banner' layout. For the 'banner' layout this text is displayed as the main headline inside the banner.

schema.label: Section Subtitle
schema.help_text: Optional smaller text shown below the section title. Leave empty to hide. For the 'banner' layout this text is shown as supporting copy below the headline inside the banner. Example: 'Catch up on what you missed'.

schema.label: Section Image
schema.help_text: Optional image for this section. Used as: (1) background for 'banner' layout, (2) hero fallback for 'showcase' when the first item has no image, (3) decorative header visual for other layouts. For 'banner' layout this is the only image — upload at least 1200x600px. For all other layouts upload at least 1200x400px. Leave empty to use the app's default brand placeholder.

schema.label: Accent Color
schema.help_text: Optional hex color that overrides the app's default primary color for this section only. Affects the section title, 'see all' button, card highlights, and dots indicator. Leave empty to use the app's global theme color. Format: '#RRGGBB' (e.g. '#E23636' for red, '#F5A623' for orange, '#00B4D8' for cyan).

schema.label: See All Button Label
schema.help_text: Text displayed on the action button next to the section title (e.g. 'Ver todo', 'See all', 'Explore'). Leave empty to hide the button entirely. For 'banner' layout this text appears as the CTA button label inside the banner.

schema.label: See All Action
schema.help_text: Destination when tapping the 'see all' button or the 'banner' CTA. Supports two formats: (1) In-app deep link using 'screen://' prefix (e.g. 'screen://catalog?filter=marvel', 'screen://search?tag=action'). (2) External URL (e.g. 'https://mi-app.com/premium'). Leave empty if see_all_label is also empty.

schema.label: Source Content Type
schema.help_text: The exact slug of the CMS content type whose records will be shown as cards (e.g. 'articles', 'sermons', 'workouts', 'movies'). Must match the content type slug exactly — case-sensitive. Leave empty only when card_type is 'banner', since banners show only the Section Image and title with no external data.

schema.label: Filter Field Key
schema.help_text: Optional. The field key in source_content_type to filter records by (e.g. 'studio', 'genre', 'category', 'type', 'featured'). Use together with filter_value. Leave both empty to show all records from the source content type without filtering. This allows multiple sections pointing to the same content type but showing different subsets — e.g. two 'movies' sections, one filtered by studio='marvel' and another by studio='pixar'.

schema.label: Filter Value
schema.help_text: The exact value to match against filter_field. Only records where filter_field equals this value will appear in this section. Case-sensitive — must match exactly as stored in the source content type (e.g. 'marvel', 'action', 'true'). Leave empty if filter_field is also empty.

schema.label: Sort Field Key
schema.help_text: The field key from source_content_type to use for ordering results (e.g. 'release_date', 'title', 'views', 'created_at'). Use together with sort_direction. Leave empty to use the CMS default order (by created_at descending).

schema.label: Sort Direction
schema.help_text: Direction for sort_field ordering. 'asc' = ascending (A→Z, oldest first, lowest number first). 'desc' = descending (Z→A, newest first, highest number first). Leave empty if sort_field is also empty.

schema.label: Max Items
schema.help_text: Maximum number of cards to load and display in this section. Defaults to 10. Recommended limits by layout: 'featured' → 5, 'large' → 10, 'small' → 15, 'image_carousel' → 8, 'stories' → 10, 'showcase' → 6, 'grid' → 12 (use even numbers for symmetry), 'banner' → 1. Keep at or below 20 for smooth scroll performance.

schema.label: Title Field Key
schema.help_text: The field key from source_content_type to display as the card title (e.g. 'headline', 'name', 'title'). Leave empty to show image-only cards with no title text — recommended for 'image_carousel' layout.

schema.label: Subtitle / Preview Field Key
schema.help_text: The field key to display as the card subtitle or preview text (e.g. 'tagline', 'summary', 'director', 'year', 'rating', 'duration'). Leave empty to hide the subtitle line. For 'stories' layout this field is ignored — only title_field appears below the circle.

schema.label: Image Field Key
schema.help_text: The key of the media field in source_content_type to use as the card image (e.g. 'poster', 'thumbnail', 'cover_image', 'backdrop', 'logo'). The app automatically resolves the URL from the CMS media field. Leave empty to fall back to the Section Image above, or a brand-color placeholder if that is also empty. Recommended upload sizes: 'featured'/'large'/'image_carousel' → min 800x450px. 'small' → min 400x400px. 'stories' → min 400x400px square.

schema.label: Category Field Key
schema.help_text: The key of the select field in source_content_type that holds the category or tags for each item (e.g. 'genre', 'tags', 'category'). Displayed as small chips on the card. Supports both single-select and multi-select fields — the app handles both automatically. Leave empty to hide category chips. Not used in 'stories' or 'image_carousel' layouts.

schema.label: Content Date Field Key
schema.help_text: The key of a date or datetime field in source_content_type to display on the card (e.g. 'release_date' for movies, 'event_date' for events, 'published_at' for articles). This is the content's own meaningful date — not the CMS system timestamp. Leave empty to hide the date on cards.

schema.label: Card Tap Action
schema.help_text: Destination when the user taps an individual card. Supports in-app deep links and external URLs. Use {id} as a placeholder — the app replaces it with the tapped item's CMS record ID at runtime. Examples: 'screen://detail/{id}' (in-app detail screen), 'screen://player/{id}' (video player), 'https://mi-app.com/content/{id}' (web fallback). Leave empty to make cards non-tappable.

data.text: How to Pack a Suitcase Like a Pro

Build a High Productivity System That Actually Works

Create a Clear Daily Plan

Productivity begins with clarity. Start each day by identifying your top priorities and writing down the most important tasks you need to complete. Focus on a short list instead of trying to do everything at once.

Use Time Blocking

Assign specific blocks of time for deep work, meetings, emails, breaks, and planning. Scheduling your day in advance reduces distractions and helps you stay consistent.

Eliminate Unnecessary Distractions

Turn off non-essential notifications, keep your workspace clean, and create an environment that supports concentration. Small interruptions can significantly reduce momentum.

Work in Focus Sessions

Use focused work intervals such as 25, 45, or 60 minutes followed by short breaks. This keeps energy levels stable and helps maintain attention throughout the day.

Track Tasks in One Trusted System

Keep all tasks, ideas, deadlines, and reminders in one place. Whether you use a notebook or digital tool, a reliable system prevents mental overload and forgotten responsibilities.

Review Progress Weekly

Take time each week to review completed tasks, unfinished priorities, and upcoming goals. Regular reviews help you improve your process and stay aligned with long-term objectives.

Protect Your Energy

Sleep well, exercise regularly, eat balanced meals, and schedule recovery time. High productivity is not only about managing time—it is also about managing energy.

Improve Continuously

A strong productivity system evolves over time. Test new methods, remove what does not work, and keep refining your routine until it feels sustainable and effective.

The best productivity system is simple, repeatable, and built around your real life.

Start With a Packing List

Before placing anything in your suitcase, make a list of essentials such as clothing, toiletries, chargers, travel documents, and medications. A checklist helps you avoid forgetting important items and prevents overpacking.

Choose the Right Clothes

Pack versatile clothing that can be mixed and matched. Choose neutral colors and lightweight fabrics that are easy to layer. This allows you to create multiple outfits with fewer pieces.

Roll Instead of Fold

Rolling clothes instead of folding them can save space and reduce wrinkles. T-shirts, jeans, casual dresses, and workout clothes are ideal for rolling.

Use Packing Cubes

Packing cubes help organize your suitcase by category. Use one for tops, one for bottoms, one for undergarments, and another for accessories. They make unpacking faster and keep everything neat.

Place Heavy Items at the Bottom

Shoes, toiletry bags, and heavier objects should be placed near the wheels or bottom of the suitcase. This helps balance the bag and makes it easier to move.

Protect Fragile Items

Wrap fragile items in soft clothing such as socks or sweaters. Place them in the center of the suitcase for extra protection.

Leave Room for Extras

Keep some empty space for souvenirs, shopping, or items you may pick up during your trip.

Keep Essentials in Your Carry-On

Always carry valuables, travel documents, medications, chargers, and one extra outfit in your carry-on bag in case your checked luggage is delayed.

Final Check

Before closing your suitcase, review your list one last time. Make sure passports, tickets, and personal items are easy to access.

With smart packing habits, every trip becomes easier, lighter, and more enjoyable.

Stay Mobile

Mobility training improves joint range of motion and movement quality. Dynamic warmups and focused stretching help athletes perform better.

Gym Mobility Routine

Duration: 20–30 minutes
Goal: Improve flexibility, joint health, range of motion, and movement quality.
Frequency: 3–5 times per week (before or after workouts)

Warm-Up (5 minutes)

  1. Light Cardio – 3 minutes
    Treadmill walk, bike, or rowing machine.

  2. Arm Circles – 30 seconds forward / 30 seconds backward

  3. Hip Circles – 30 seconds each direction

  4. Ankle Rolls – 20 seconds each ankle

Full Body Mobility Routine

Upper Body

  1. Thoracic Spine Rotations – 2 sets x 10 reps each side
    On all fours, place one hand behind head and rotate upward.

  2. Shoulder Dislocates (with band or stick) – 2 sets x 12 reps

  3. Wall Slides – 2 sets x 12 reps

Lower Body

  1. Deep Squat Hold – 3 sets x 30 seconds
    Keep chest up and heels down.

  2. World’s Greatest Stretch – 2 sets x 5 reps each side

  3. 90/90 Hip Rotations – 2 sets x 10 reps

  4. Walking Lunges with Twist – 2 sets x 10 steps each side

Ankles / Knees

  1. Knee Over Toe Ankle Rocks – 2 sets x 15 reps each side

  2. Calf Stretch Against Wall – 2 sets x 30 seconds each side

Core / Control

  1. Cat-Cow Stretch – 2 sets x 10 reps

  2. Dead Bug – 2 sets x 12 reps

Cool Down (Optional)

  • Child’s Pose – 30 sec

  • Hamstring Stretch – 30 sec each leg

  • Cobra Stretch – 30 sec

If You Lift Weights Often

Use this before workouts:

  • Hip mobility before leg day

  • Shoulder + thoracic mobility before upper body day

  • Ankles + hips before squats

Quick 10-Minute Version

  • Deep Squat Hold

  • 90/90 Hips

  • Thoracic Rotations

  • World’s Greatest Stretch

  • Ankle Rocks

(2 rounds)

Tip

Move slowly and controlled. Mobility is about strength through range of motion, not just stretching.
